questions.q: What kinds of changes happen around us?
questions.a: Fast and slow changes, reversible and irreversible, physical and chemical.

questions.q: Classify burning of a candle - physical or chemical?
questions.a: Both occur: wax melting is physical, but burning wax to CO2 and soot is chemical.

questions.q: Give one slow change and one fast change in nature.
questions.a: Slow: rusting of iron. Fast: lightning, or tearing of paper.
A change of shape, size or state with no new substance, usually reversible.
Melting ice and dissolving sugar (also folding paper).

questions.q: Does a physical change make a new material? Explain.
questions.a: No - the substance stays the same, only its form changes, and it can be undone.
New substances with new properties form, often with colour change, gas, heat or light.

questions.q: Give two examples of chemical changes in the kitchen.
questions.a: Cooking an egg and milk turning to curd.

questions.q: Why can most chemical changes not be reversed?
questions.a: The original substances react to form different materials; undoing them needs other reactions.

questions.q: What are slow changes? Give two examples.
questions.a: Changes taking days, months or years - rusting of iron and germination of a seed.

questions.q: What are desirable and undesirable changes? Give one each.
questions.a: Desirable: cooking food. Undesirable: souring of milk.

questions.q: Classify the bursting of a firecracker as fast/slow and chemical/physical.
questions.a: Fast and chemical - new gases and light form in a flash.
